title: The Videha kingdom & King Janaka
body: Mithila rises as the kingdom of Videha, ruled by a line of philosopher-kings titled 'Janaka'. The court of King Janaka — father of Sita — draws sages such as Yajnavalkya and Gargi.

title: From kingdom to republic
body: After the monarchy ends, Videha becomes part of the Vajji confederacy centred on Vaishali — among the earliest experiments in republican government.

title: Mahavira & the age of the great teachers
body: Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara, is born (traditionally in the 6th century BCE) at Kundagrama near Vaishali, in the Vajji republic. The Buddha too preaches and spends rains-retreats at Vaishali, making the Mithila plains a cradle of India's new philosophies.

title: Absorbed by Magadha
body: Ajatashatru of Magadha defeats the Vajji league; Mithila is folded into the Magadhan empire.

title: The Karnat dynasty
body: Nanyadeva founds the Karnat dynasty with its capital at Simraungadh on today's India–Nepal border, beginning a cultural golden age.

title: Varna Ratnakara & the Panji
body: Jyotirishwar Thakur writes the Varna Ratnakara — the oldest Maithili prose, and among the earliest prose in any modern Indian language. The Panji genealogical system is instituted.

title: The Oiniwar dynasty & Vidyapati
body: Under the Maithil-Brahmin Oiniwar kings, the poet Vidyapati composes his Padavali, transforming Maithili into a literary language.

title: The Darbhanga Raj
body: Mahesh Thakur, granted authority by Emperor Akbar, founds the Khandavala (Darbhanga Raj) dynasty — which becomes the largest and richest zamindari of north Bihar.

title: The Treaty of Sugauli
body: The Anglo-Nepalese War ends; the treaty fixes the border that splits historic Mithila between British India and Nepal.

title: The Tirhut Railway
body: Maharaja Lakshmeshwar Singh launches the Tirhut Railway, often called India's first private railway, alongside schools, hospitals and famine relief.

title: Janaki Mandir at Janakpur
body: Queen Vrisha Bhanu of Tikamgarh funds the great marble Janaki Mandir on the spot held to be Sita's home — the grandest temple of the Mithila world and the heart of modern Janakpur.

title: Maithili recognised by the Sahitya Akademi
body: India's national academy of letters formally recognises Maithili as an independent literary language; the first Akademi award for Maithili follows in 1966.

title: Maithili enters the Eighth Schedule
body: The 92nd Constitutional Amendment adds Maithili to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, granting it official recognition after a long campaign.

title: Mithila Makhana wins a GI tag
body: Mithila Makhana receives a Geographical Indication tag, protecting the fox-nut that grows in the region's ponds and accounts for the bulk of India's production.

title: Bharat Ratna for Karpoori Thakur
body: Karpoori Thakur, the 'Jan Nayak' and twice Chief Minister of Bihar, is awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously — a rare national honour for a son of the region's backward-caste movement.

title: The statehood demand endures
body: The long-running campaign for a separate Mithila state resurfaces in public debate, alongside calls for classical-language status for Maithili.
